summary.intent: Run load tests against the staging API with 10, 20, and 30 concurrent clients to establish performance baselines, then scale up to determine the maximum reliable client count for a single instance.
summary.outcome: 10/20/30-client baselines were collected (zero errors, near-linear scaling) and documented. 50/75/100-client runs were triggered but cancelled due to a 30-minute job timeout caused by a broken scenario filter running all 5 test scenarios instead of just mixed-workload. Two fix PRs were created: #337 (fixing --testPathPattern Jest flag and missing environment: staging) which merged, and #339 (fixing scenario filter, adding concurrency group, bumping timeout to 60m) which was pending rename to chore(ci) at session end.

repo: The load test workflow uses GitHub Actions environment-scoped secrets under 'staging' environment — declaring environment: staging on a job causes the UI to show 'Deploying to staging' even when no deployment occurs; this is purely cosmetic.

The uploadFile operation in the SDK is actually 5 sequential API calls: 3x POST /ipfs/upload (ciphertext, file metadata, folder metadata) + 2x POST /ipns/publish — so SDK-measured latency is the sum of all five.

Prometheus metrics available for upload flow analysis: cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds{operation='pin'}, cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds{route='/ipfs/upload'}, cipherbox_http_request_duration_seconds{route='/ipns/publish'}, cipherbox_ipns_publish_duration_seconds.
Baseline docs live at .planning/baselines/ with a numbered phase convention (e.g. 19-someguy-ipns-baselines.md); a dedicated branch 'docs/phase-19-baselines' exists for these.

10/20/30-client mixed-workload staging results: 434/856/1299 total ops, 0 errors, 4.49/8.42/12.14 ops/sec — near-linear scaling with modest latency growth (~15-25% p50 increase from 10 to 30 clients).
The load-test.yml job had a 30-minute timeout which is insufficient when all 5 scenarios run — 10-client all-scenarios run took 16 minutes alone.

code.finding: The test:single npm script used --testPathPattern which is a Jest CLI flag not recognized by Vitest. Vitest uses positional args for file filtering. Fixed by removing the flag.

Passing scenario via 'pnpm test:single -- <scenario>' does not work — CAC (Vitest's CLI parser) puts args after -- into a separate bucket, not the file filter list. Must call 'pnpm exec vitest run --no-coverage <scenario>' directly.
Job was missing 'environment: staging' declaration, causing all staging-scoped secrets (STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET) and vars (STAGING_API_URL) to be empty.

workflow: Running multiple 'gh run watch' instances simultaneously at 3-second polling intervals (6 watchers = ~120 req/min = 7200/hr) easily exceeds GitHub's 5000 req/hour API rate limit.
gh run watch exits early when a job hits a deployment environment approval step, giving a false 'completed' signal before the actual test job finishes.
Concurrent load test runs against the same staging API will interfere with each other's results — a concurrency group (load-test-<environment>) should be used to queue runs serially.
Commits that should not trigger release-please must use conventional commit prefixes like chore(ci) rather than fix() or feat().

friction: First batch of 10/20/30-client runs all failed immediately due to two bugs: --testPathPattern (Jest flag in Vitest project) and missing environment: staging declaration on the job.

Scenario filter via npm script passthrough ('--') was silently broken — all 5 scenarios ran instead of just mixed-workload, causing 50/75/100-client runs to exceed the 30-minute timeout and get cancelled.
Multiple gh run watch instances triggered a GitHub API rate limit that persisted for the remainder of the session, blocking status checks.
gh run watch prematurely exiting due to the deployment environment step created confusion about which task IDs were 'real' watchers vs stale ones.
PR #337 fix branch was created off an old base, requiring a new branch after the PR merged.
The session ended with PR #339 needing a branch/commit rename to chore(ci) before merging — an additional step required to avoid triggering release-please.
open_items: PR #339 needs to be merged (after renaming branch/commit to chore(ci) prefix) before 50/75/100-client runs can be re-triggered.
50/75/100-client mixed-workload runs still need to be executed to determine the single-instance capacity ceiling.
Deep-dive into uploadFile latency breakdown using staging Prometheus metrics and logs is planned but blocked until the higher client-count runs complete.
The 'Deploying to staging' label cosmetic issue was accepted as-is, but an alternative (moving secrets to repo-level) was noted if it becomes a problem.
GitHub API rate limit was still active at session end — polling strategy needs to be revisited (single status check instead of continuous watch, or longer polling interval).
